cards.explanation: The answer is to drive them all out. The LORD says, "…you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land…" (Numbers 33:52). Not some of them. All of them. When the LORD gives Moses an instruction, He doesn't leave a loose end hanging around like a stray crumb.

The answer is destroy. The LORD tells Israel to "…destroy all their carved images and cast idols…" (Numbers 33:52). Those idols aren't going home as souvenirs, friends. The command is clear and it's the whole job.

The answer is False. The LORD says Israel must "…demolish all their high places." (Numbers 33:52). He lists it right alongside their carved images and cast idols. The instruction is to take the high places down, so no leaving a few up for decoration.

The answer is that He has given them the land. The LORD says, "…for I have given you the land to possess." (Numbers 33:53). The reason is that He gave it, plain and simple. When the LORD hands you the keys, that's the whole reason, friends.

The answer is by casting lots. The LORD says, "…you are to divide the land by lot according to your clans." (Numbers 33:54). Then He adds, "Whatever falls to each one by lot will be his." So the lot is what settles each share, and nobody has to guess whose it is.

The answer is True! The LORD says, "Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one." (Numbers 33:54). Nobody gets a share by shouting the loudest, and nobody gets one by being first in line. The size of the clan sets the size of the share. And the LORD adds that whatever falls to each one by lot will be his. I wish my cookie boxes sorted themselves that fairly.

The answer is harass. The LORD says those left in the land "…will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides; they will harass you in the land where you settle." (Numbers 33:55). Barbs and thorns aren't comfy things to carry around, friends. That's a warning with some sting to it.

The answer is that He will do to Israel what He had planned for Canaan. The LORD says, "And then I will do to you what I had planned to do to them." (Numbers 33:56). It's a serious line, so I'll let it be serious. The warning is real, and it comes with that big IF.

The answer is that the other tribes already have their land. Moses says, "For the tribes of the Reubenites and Gadites, along with the half-tribe of Manasseh, have already received their inheritance." (Numbers 34:14). That leaves nine and a half tribes still waiting on their shares. The math works out, even with a half in it.

The answer is True. Moses says, "These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, toward the sunrise." (Numbers 34:15). Those tribes are Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh. Their land sits on the east side of the river.

The answer is Eleazar and Joshua, friends! The LORD says, "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 34:17). Eleazar is a priest, and Joshua is named as the son of Nun. Two names on the job list, and then He tells Moses to appoint one leader from each tribe to help distribute the land (Numbers 34:18). That's a whole team, and I'd want my name on that list.

The answer is tribe. The LORD says, "Appoint one leader from each tribe to distribute the land." (Numbers 34:18). Every tribe gets someone of its own at the table. Nobody has to hope the other tribes remembered them.
